sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205], but the path was a step change, not a straight line.
Revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021 [D183][D230], then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in FY2023 through FY2025 [D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 step came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase as the pandemic shifted spending toward the stores [P51][P55].
The recent decline reflects a 2.6% comparable sales decrease in FY2025, split between 2.2% lower traffic and 0.4% lower average transaction [P14].
Merchandise sales are 98.0% of revenue in FY2025 [D465], so the category mix inside that line is the whole growth story.
Food & beverage grew to 23.0% of revenue in FY2025 from 19.6% in FY2017 [D484][D506], adding 0.3pp of growth in FY2025 while apparel fell 4.7% and subtracted 0.7pp [D508][D564][D565].
The filings attribute the FY2023 sales decline to weakness in discretionary categories, partly offset by frequency categories [P30], and that mix shift has persisted.
Operating income grew only 0.6% a year over the window against 4.5% revenue growth [F207][F205], so there was no operating leverage across the decade.
EPS diluted compounded at 6.3% against 3.4% net income growth [F210][F208], as diluted shares fell from 582.5 million to 455.6 million [X107][X116].
Operating margin was 4.9% in FY2025 [F34], below the 5.6% window median [D590] and far under the 8.4% FY2021 high [D589].
The FY2025 margin fell 0.3pp [D429], with cost of revenue taking 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D440][D441].
The gross margin rate slipped to 27.9% from 28.2% [P12], while the SG&A rate held at 20.6% only because of a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit [P11].
The largest move was FY2022, when operating margin fell 4.9pp [D290] as cost of revenue took 4.6pp [D301].
That year's margin compression came from promotional and clearance markdowns, excess inventory removal and higher supply-chain costs [P38].
Operating cash flow was 1.77x net income in FY2025 [D404], below the 2.01x window median [D619], and free cash flow was 0.77x net income [D405].
The FY2025 operating cash flow decline reflects lower net earnings and lower accounts payable leverage [P7].
Free cash flow margin was 2.7% in FY2025 [D401], under the 4.5% window median [D596] and the 4.2% retail peer median [D611].
Capex was 3.6% of revenue and 1.19x D&A in FY2025 [D400][D406], up from 2.7% of revenue in FY2024 [D354].
The capex increase reflects more spending on new stores and remodels [P5], and management guides to about $5 billion in FY2026 [P4].
Cash was $5.49 billion against $14.4 billion of long-term debt in FY2025 [F144][F194], leaving the company in net debt.
The current ratio was 0.94x [F184], equal to the 0.94x window median [D602] and above the 0.83x FY2018 low [D600].
Return on average equity was 24.0% [D415], below the 28.6% retail peer median [D617].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.46 billion were 86.8% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D412][D413], and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D434].
Revenue has fallen three years running, from $109.1 billion in FY2022 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [R1][F7][F10], a 1.3% three-year CAGR [D603].
The decline is traffic-led, with FY2025 comparable sales down 2.6% on a 2.2% traffic drop [P14], which matters because it erodes fixed-cost leverage.
The current ratio sits at 0.94x [R2][F184], meaning current liabilities of $21.2 billion exceed current assets of $20.0 billion [F164][F154].
Operating margin has fallen two years in a row, 0.4pp in total, to 4.9% [R4][F32][F34].

Data-quality note: short-term investments are already inside cash [R7][F144][X170], and the FY2016-FY2018 current debt portion is inside long-term debt [R8][X177][X173], so net-cash figures are excluded here.
Operating margin: a print below the 4.9% FY2025 level [F34] would extend the two-year slide, while a recovery above the 5.6% window median [D590] would reverse it; the FY2026 10-K will show it.

Free cash flow margin: holding at or above the 4.5% window median [D596] would confirm cash generation, while a drop toward the 2.7% FY2025 level [D401] would not; watch the FY2026 cash flow statement.
Capex: spending near the guided $5 billion [P4] against FY2025's $3.73 billion [F94] would keep free cash flow under pressure; the FY2026 10-K will report the actual figure.
